 lifetime ISA. Lifetime ISA mistakes.
subtitles: You shouldn't get a lifetime ISA. The government does give you a 25% bonus, but here are the four reasons why it doesn't actually work out the way you think it does. Number one, the withdrawal penalty is worse than you think. If you need the money before you're 60 or can't use it for your first home, then you will effectively lose the bonus and an additional 6.25%. The second thing if you choose to use it for a property, it needs to be under £450,000. Money Saving Expert did research on this and especially if you live in London, it's very unlikely that you're able to get something under £450,000 that you would actually use. So now you're probably thinking oh, I'll just use it for retirement, but you're actually better off salary sacrificing into your pension instead. If you're a basic rate taxpayer, you're saving 20% on your tax, 8% on National Insurance, and if you have student loans, you're also saving on the student loan contributions as well. That means you're getting a 37% bonus by putting into your pension instead of a 20% bonus by putting into your lifetime ISA. Lastly, there is a 12 month rules. If you are using it for a property under 450,000, you need to make sure that your account has been open for at least a year. So if you're opening a lifetime ISA, please make sure that the property that you're planning to buy is under 450,000. Otherwise You're better off using other accounts. (Nuanced notes below 👇 ) This is the framework I use to determine which accounts I prioritize first. How do you prioritize your accounts?

The nuanced version:
1. Emergency fund. Keep it in a HYSA or if it’s large (above £10k) consider a cash ISA.

2.Employer match pension. Take advantage of the bonus you get from your employer. Opting out is giving yourself a pay cut for no reason.

3. Individual Savings Accounts. This could be S&S ISA or LISA, or both. How you want to prioritize depends on your goals and the property you are looking for.

4. SIPP. You do get the tax savings here. Ideally if your employer offers a salary sacrifice, I would do that instead to save on National Insurance and student loan contributions.

5. General account. If you’ve maxed out everything above, it’s time to just use a general account. There’s no tax benefits here so just keep that in mind.

Why the stock market is down. Stock market strategies. Panic buying and selling. Is now a good time to invest. Lump sum investing. DCA. Dollar cost averaging.
subtitles: I've lost £20K this month and about to put in another £3.5k. Here's why. With the stock market generally down and the conflicting news that's coming out every other hour, I have been debating on whether to put extra money in. The answer is yes, but not for the reasons that you think. Most people think that buying the dip is about time in the market, so buying low and selling high. But research has consistently shown that time in the market is near impossible. Nobody, including the Wall Street investors, can predict the bottom. So really, if you're waiting for the bottom, you're already losing, and you're effectively just gambling. The safer approach is probably doing a DCA Method, or dollar cost averaging. This is where you invest the same amount at a regular interval so the highs and lows eventually even out and you're not too affected by the volatility in the short term. But this also technically isn't the best strategy. Statistically speaking, putting a lump sum money in as early as possible will always win. Time in the market beats timing the market for me, My anxiety cannot handle that. So here's what I'm gonna be doing. I'm gonna be doing a modified dollar cost averaging where I'll be putting more currently in these couple next months just to take advantage of the stock market being down. This way I don't feel like I'm gonna lose all my money, but I'm still able To take advantage of the lower prices, what are your strategies during this downturn? no bake biscoff cheesecake 🍰🤎
ingredients:
2 packs of biscoff cookies 
12 tbsp salted butter melted 
1.5 tbsp light brown sugar 

24 oz cream cheese (room temperature)
1/2 cup powdered sugar 
1/2 cup biscoff spread 
1 tbsp vanilla extract 

1 1/2 cups heavy whipping cream 
1/2 cup powdered sugar 

1/3 cup biscoff spread melted 
6 biscoff cookies crushed
2 biscoff cookies for topping

instructions 🍰 
place 2 packs of biscoff cookies into a blender or food processor and blend until they form fine crumbs.
in a springform pan, combine the cookie crumbs with 1.5 tbsp of brown sugar, and 12 tbsp of melted butter.
mix until the texture resembles wet sand and the crumbs clump when pressed.
press the mixture firmly into the bottom of the pan, slightly pressing some crumbs up the side to create the crust.
place in the refrigerator for 30 minutes so the crust can firm up.

in a large bowl beat 24 oz of room temperature cream cheese until smooth.
add in 1/2 cup of biscoff spread, 1 tbsp vanilla extract, and 1/2 cup of powdered sugar.
mix together until silky.

in a separate bowl, whip together 1/2 cups of heavy cream and 1/2 cup of powdered sugar.
gently fold in the whipped cream into the cream cheese filling. do not over mix 
spread the cheesecake filling evenly over the chilled crust and smooth the top. refrigerate overnight until fully set.

melt 1/3 cup of the biscoff spread.
pour it over the cold cheesecake and gently spread it to the edges. place back in the fridge for 30 minutes to set the biscoff topping.

crush about 6 biscoff cookies and place it around the edges of the cheesecake.
add 2 full biscoff cookies to the top of your cheesecake.
slice and serve chilled

subtitles: I feel like people on here give really generic advice just because it's easy to do, but that doesn't necessarily help anyone. And now that i'm older, there's definitely a lot of things I could have been told earlier on that would have saved me a lot of time. The first is that credibility beats out potential every time. If you learn to establish credibility early on, you will make your life significantly easier. And there's a few ways to establish credibility, but the best ways, in my opinion, are creating or starting something from scratch and seeing it through to completion or success. The second way is leading something from ideation to completion or success. Proving that you can actually do something outweighs the potential of you being able to do something. Another thing I wish I was told is that you always need a factor in the chance that you may fail or be bad at something. And the quicker you identify that you aren't good at it or that you failed at it and pivot, you save yourself a lot of time. And the last thing is, if you're looking for guidance or mentorship, just make sure that person does things the right way. Being guided by someone that cuts corners will never work out for you, because when you're presented with something that actually takes hard work, you're not gonna know how to function.

people think getting in shape means going from 0 → 100 overnight. Two hour workouts. Training every day. Completely changing your diet. And then when it becomes overwhelming… they quit.

Real progress usually looks much simpler.

It’s going for a walk when you didn’t feel like it.
It’s doing a 20 to 30 minute workout instead of skipping it.
It’s choosing consistency even when the workout isn’t perfect.

Fitness isn’t about being intense for a week.
It’s about showing up in small ways over and over again.

Those small habits compound into real results.

So if you’re starting your fitness journey, don’t focus on doing everything. Focus on doing something consistently.

Consistency will always beat intensity you can’t maintain.

How to study like Japanese students‼️

📓 Kaizen mindset
Japanese students focus on small daily improvement. Even thirty minutes every day beats random long study days. Consistency over intensity always wins.

🧠 Shūkanika meaning habit building
They rely on routine, not motivation. Same study time, same place, same flow. Your brain learns to focus automatically.

✏️ Kaki nagara manabu meaning learn by writing
Instead of just reading, they write summaries, formulas, and explanations again and again. Writing locks information into memory.

📖 Fukushū meaning revision
Revision is non negotiable. They revise the same topic multiple times in short sessions instead of cramming once.

⏳ Shōjikan shūchū meaning short focused study
They study in short, distraction free blocks. Deep focus for a short time beats distracted long hours.

🧹 Seiri seiton meaning organised space
A clean desk is part of studying. Minimal setup reduces mental noise and improves concentration.

🎒 Yoshuu meaning pre study
Before class, they lightly preview topics. This makes understanding in class much easier and reduces stress later.

📘 Mondai renshū meaning practice questions
Practice is more important than rereading. Solving questions daily is how concepts actually stick.

😴 Jūbun na suimin meaning proper sleep
They protect sleep because tired brains cannot learn. Studying late is useless if retention drops.

How to study daily without stress‼️

🧠 Keep your daily goals small and clear
Stress usually comes from unrealistic plans. Decide exactly what you will study that day and keep it limited. Finishing a small task daily builds confidence and removes pressure.

📚 Study at a fixed time every day
When studying has a fixed slot, your brain stops negotiating. You don’t waste energy deciding when to study, which automatically lowers stress.

⏳ Use focused but short sessions
Daily studying is about consistency, not long hours. Short focused sessions help you stay fresh and avoid mental fatigue.

✏️ Study actively, not passively
Reading again and again creates stress because nothing feels clear. Solving questions, writing summaries, and explaining concepts make learning feel controlled and effective.

📖 Revise a little every day
Small daily revision prevents topics from piling up. When nothing feels forgotten, exam fear drops naturally.

🧹 Keep your study space simple
Clutter increases mental load. A clean desk and minimal setup help your mind stay calm and organised.

📱 Control distractions before you start
Put your phone away and close extra tabs. Fewer distractions mean smoother study sessions and less frustration.

😌 End with a light task
Finish your study session with something easy. This leaves your brain feeling accomplished instead of drained.

🛌 Take care of your body
Good sleep, water, and proper meals support daily focus. A rested body handles studying with far less stress.

‼️How to study and actually remember

🧠 After you study something, close the book and try to remember it without looking. It will feel messy and uncomfortable, but that struggle is exactly how your brain learns to remember.

✍️ Take a blank page and write whatever you remember from the topic. Don’t worry about order or neatness. This shows you what actually stayed in your head.

🔄 Instead of finishing one chapter in one go, switch between two similar topics. It feels harder, but your brain remembers better when it learns to tell things apart.

⏱️ Don’t revise immediately. Come back to the topic after a few hours. That small gap makes the memory stick longer.

🗺️ Try studying the same subject in the same spot every day. Over time, just sitting there will put your brain into study mode.

🎧 Record yourself explaining the topic like you’re teaching a friend. Listen to it later while walking or resting. It feels weird, but it works.

🧩 Attempt questions before you feel “ready.” Getting things wrong first actually helps your brain understand faster.

🧠 Force yourself to shrink the topic into a few main ideas. If you can’t explain it simply, you probably haven’t understood it yet.

🛌 Read a short summary before sleeping, then test yourself the next morning. Sleep does half the remembering for you.

caption:
13yr-Old Lucas, became 1st person in history to Beat! Terminal Brain Cancer!!!

#braincancer #cancer #cancersucks #cancersurvivor #awareness
subtitles: Lucas changed the history of brain cancer and exposed a broken system. For decades, brain cancer, especially rare childhood forms like diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma, D I P G, has been one of the most devastating diagnoses in medicine. Children were routinely told they had months to live, not because doctors didn't care, but because science had no effective treatments and the system failed to prioritise these rare cases. In the United States, cancer treatment is a massive industry. Cancer drugs generate tens of billions of dollars every year, with projections reaching hundreds of billions globally in the coming decade. However, brain cancers represent only a small fraction of that revenue, roughly a few billion dollars annually, and rare pediatric brain cancers like D I P G. Account for only a tiny slice of that already small portion. Because these cancers affect relatively few patients and are biologically complex, they historically received less research funding, fewer drug trials, and slower progress. That context matters. At age 6, Lucas, a Belgian child, was diagnosed with D I P G, a cancer where most children do not survive a year. His family was told to prepare for the worst. Instead of accepting that fate, they travelled to France, where Lucas was enrolled in the Biomed clinical trial at the Gustave Roussy Cancer Centre. What happened next changed medical history. Lucas responded dramatically to the drug everolimus, not because it was a guaranteed cure, but because his tumor carried an extremely rare genetic mutation, That made it uniquely vulnerable. Over time, M R I. Scans showed something doctors had never seen before. The tumor completely disappeared. Today, Lucas is 13 years old, cancer free, living a normal life and no longer on treatment. He is the first known child in the world to be cured of this form of brain cancer. This breakthrough did not come from profit driven medicine. It came from public research, international collaboration, long term trials, and scientists willing to study children even when success wasn't guaranteed. Lucas's case is now guiding new research that could one day help other children. But doctors are clear. Turning this discovery into a widely available treatment will still take 10, 15 years. Lucas's story proves something important. Not that cures were hidden, not that doctors refused to help, but that rare childhood cancers were underserved in a system driven by scale, speed, and return on investment. Lucas didn't just survive. He rewrote what was thought possible. And his life stands as both a victory and a reminder that when science, funding, and compassion finally align, even the most incurable cancers can fall.

caption:
Lottery: A Life-Changing Dream or a Financial Trap?

#lottery #info #wealth #fyp #documentary
subtitles: Every day in the United States, the lottery quietly moves more money than most people realise. On average, Americans spend roughly $300 million a day on lottery tickets. That comes out to well over $100 billion a year. It is one of the most consistent cash flows in the country. Not because the odds are good, but because hope is powerful, especially when people feel stuck, stressed, or financially desperate. The lottery thrives in moments of pressure when wages lag, debt rises, and the future feels uncertain. A few dollars for a ticket feels like relief. It feels like a shortcut. But mathematically, the lottery is designed so that the vast majority of players lose over and over again. The odds of winning a major Powerball Jackpot are about 1 in 292 million. That is not a strategy that is a long shot sold as a dream. When people do win, the picture is very different from what most imagine. The average large Jackpot winner is not a young person starting life. Studies and surveys of winners consistently place the average age in the early to mid 50s. Many winners have already lived most of their working lives. That alone changes how the money actually impacts their future. Certain states appear to win more, but that perception is driven by population and ticket sales, not luck. States like California, Florida, New York, Texas, and historically, Indiana show up often simply because they sell more tickets. More tickets means more winners. There is no magic state No lucky region, just volume. The part rarely advertised is what happens after the cameras leave. While the viral claim that most winners go broke is exaggerated, the reality is still uncomfortable. A significant minority of big winners eventually face serious financial trouble. Some declare bankruptcy. Others lose relationships, privacy, or peace of mind. The money exposes weaknesses that were already there and adds pressure that most people are not trained to handle. There are infamous stories that illustrate the dark side. Billy Bob Harold junior, a Texas winner, gave generously to family, friends and strangers until the money and the pressure collapsed his life. Abraham Shakespeare won millions in Florida and was later murdered by someone who manipulated and exploited him. These are extreme cases, but they are real and they reveal a pattern. Sudden money attracts sudden problems. Many winners do fine. Some improve their quality of life, help their families responsibly, and live more comfortably without imploding. The difference is not luck. It is structure, pacing and restraint. This is where the choice between lump sum and increments, also called an annuity, becomes critical. The advertised Jackpot is almost always the annuity value paid out over 20 to 30 years. The lump sum is much smaller upfront. On top of that, a lump sum creates a massive tax hit in a single year. Federal withholding A loan starts at 24%, but top winners often owe closer to 37% federally plus state taxes depending on where they live. What looks like hundreds of millions on paper can shrink dramatically before it ever reaches a bank account. Incremental payments spread the money and the taxes over decades. They create enforced discipline. You cannot spend money you have not received yet. That pacing protects winners from reckless early decisions, bad investments, predatory advisors, and emotional spending fueled by shock and pressure. Increments turn one win into long term income, sometimes for life. Instead of a single explosive moment, people still choose the lump sum, and most winners do. They want control. They distrust long term payouts. They believe they can invest better themselves. They want to pay everything off immediately. They are surrounded by people urging them to act fast. The problem is that speed is what destroys them. Too much money too quickly, with no buffer for mistakes. Responsible gambling means understanding that the lottery is entertainment, not a financial plan. If someone plays, it should be with strict limits, never with money needed for bills, and never as a response to desperation. Chasing losses is how people quietly fall into financial holes. If someone ever does win, the steps matter more than the Celebration. The ticket should be signed immediately and secured. The win should not be announced publicly without legal advice. A lawyer should come first to handle privacy and claim structure. A tax professional should follow immediately. Spending should pause. Family help should be structured, not emotional, and the default choice should be increments, not lump Sum the lottery has a good side. It funds programs. It creates rare opportunities. It can change lives for the better. But it also has an ugly side. Built on desperation, unrealistic expectations, and financial ignorance. The system always wins. A few people get lucky, and those who survive the win are almost always the ones who slow the money down. If you ever win, do not rush. Take the increments. Let time work for you instead of against you. Decades of stability. Beat one fast check that disappears. And if you never win, remember this. The safest way to beat the lottery is not to believe it will save you.

caption:
How Billionaires Live Tax-Free (Legally)

#billionaire #information #tax #law #fyp
subtitles: Ever wonder why your favourite billionaires aren't taxed like you and me? Yeah, the people who somehow pay a lower effective tax rate than a teacher or a nurse, yet own jets, yachts, and five houses. And no, it's not because they're hiding piles of cash in a vault somewhere. Here's the part most people miss. Billionaires don't actually have most of their money in cash. Their wealth lives in assets. Stocks, companies, real estate. Things that grow in value but aren't taxed until they're sold. And since our tax system taxes income you receive, not wealth you hold, they can legally avoid triggering taxes for years, sometimes decades. So I know what you're wondering. If they don't have cash, how are they affording all these luxuries? Simple. They don't spend their wealth, they borrow against it. When you own billions in assets, banks will happily loan you millions at extremely low interest, using those assets as collateral. That loan money isn't considered income, so it's not taxed. That's what pays for the mansions, private jets, yachts, and luxury lifestyles. Perfectly legal, perfectly normal at that level. Meanwhile, if you and I want money, we have to work for it, get paid, and get taxed immediately. There's no borrowing against our future paycheck to live tax free. That's the difference. Wealth creates leverage, and leverage creates access to money without triggering taxes. And here's where it really gets interesting. Because they rarely sell those assets, they avoid capital gains taxes. Altogether, then when they die, the law allows something called a stepped up basis, which resets the value of those assets to current market prices. Translation their heirs can sell with little or no tax on decades of growth. The system quietly wipes the slate clean. This isn't a conspiracy. It's not illegal, it's not secret. It's written into the tax code and openly used by the ultra wealthy. The reason it feels unfair is because it kind of is. The system was designed around income, not extreme asset based wealth. And the ultra rich know exactly how to play within those rules. So when people ask why don't we just tax billionaires? The real answer isn't that we can't. It's that the way their money works is completely different from how yours does. And until that changes, they'll keep living lavishly, borrowing tax free and paying less, while the rest of us get taxed the moment our paycheck hits.

caption: 15 Million Vacant Homes in the US! #homes #homeless #crisis #property #foryoupage
subtitles: Did you know there are about 15 million vacant homes in the U. S? It sounds shocking, but there's an important detail people miss. The U S. Census Bureau shows that the largest share of vacant homes are seasonal, vacation or second properties, not houses just sitting there waiting for families. Once you remove those, the picture changes. We're left with year round vacant homes, and even then only a tiny portion are actually on the market at a given time. The census reported a homeowner vacancy rate of about 1.2%. That's the slice of homes truly available for sale in the homeowner inventory. That's extremely tight supply. So why are homes still empty while people struggle to buy? Many are tied up in probate, legal disputes or need major repairs. Others are held off the market by owners or investors waiting for better prices. Some sellers refuse to lower prices after years of rising home values and today's higher mortgage rates make buyers back off. There's also rate lock in where owners with ultra low pandemic mortgage rates don't wanna sell and take on a higher one. And why not just sell cheap? Because for many owners, cheap means losing money after maintenance, taxes or renovations. It can hurt neighbourhood property values and investors often prefer to wait rather than accept a loss. Housing is treated like an asset first, shelter second. Japan faces a similar but even larger issue. The country had around 9 million vacant homes, about 13.8% of Housing as of 2023, according to Japan's Ministry of Internal Affairs and communications. But unlike the U S, Japan has expanded IKEA banks, local government programs listing empty homes, sometimes for extremely low prices, while offering tax breaks and renovation subsidies to get people to move in and restore them. Could the U S. Do something similar? Financially, large scale housing programs are possible, but the challenge here is legal and structural. Property rights are strong, housing policy is split across thousands of local governments, and many vacant homes aren't publicly owned. Turning them into affordable housing would require incentives, tax changes, rehabilitation, funding, and coordination on a scale the U S. Rarely achieves. Still, with homelessness and affordability crisis growing, the bigger question isn't whether America can afford to act, it's whether it chooses to treat housing as essential infrastructure instead of just an investment.

The victims of Jonestown were not simply participants in a strange event. Many were people searching for hope, safety, and belonging. Their lives were taken through manipulation, fear, and the abuse of trust by a leader who held complete control over the community. Their story remains a powerful reminder of how dangerous unchecked power and manipulation can become.

caption:
Why Billionaires Pay Less Taxes Than You?

#billionaires #tax #wealthy #unfair #fyp
subtitles: Hey, have you ever wondered why people like Elon Musk, Bill Gates, Jeff Bezos and Mark Zuckerberg, the billionaires, the so called 1%, often seem to pay less in taxes than everyday working people? It feels backwards. You work, you get taxed right out of your paycheck, while some of the richest people report relatively low taxable income. So what happened? A major part of that answer goes back to Ronald Reagan and the shift in economic policy during the 1980s. Before Reagan, under leaders like Jimmy Carter, the top federal tax rate was as high as 70%, meaning the wealthiest Americans were taxed heavily on income. Reagan introduced supply side economics, which argued that cutting taxes, especially for businesses and high earners, would boost investment and grow the economy. In 1981, he cut the top tax rate to 50%, and by 1986 it dropped to 28%, one of the biggest reductions in U S. History. But the real shift was not just lower rates, it was how money is taxed. Most working people earn wages, which are taxed immediately. Billionaires build wealth through assets like stocks and investments, and those gains are not taxed unless they are sold. So when their wealth grows by billions, it is often considered unrealized gains, meaning no sale, no tax. On top of that, many use legal strategies like borrowing against their assets, giving them access to cash without triggering income taxes. Reagan did not create today's system alone, but his policies marked a turning Point lowering taxes at the top and reshaping how wealth is treated. Over time, this helped create a system where income from work is taxed more consistently than wealth from investments. So when people say billionaires pay less taxes, it is not always about breaking rules. It is about how the system is designed. And that design started shifting decades ago.

And even if she did, there's not enough money in the world to give someone those years back. Gary Dodson spent years behind bars before his accuser, Kathleen Crowell Webb, recanted exposing the false claim. Anthony Broadwater lost over 16 years of his life after a wrongful accusation and was only cleared decades later. And while he later received a settlement, there's not enough money in the world to restore that lost time, reputation, and peace. These situations show a real gap in accountability, because when someone lies about a crime this serious, the consequences for the accused don't just disappear. When the truth comes out, years are lost that can never be returned. At the same time, real victims already struggle to come forward, which is why this conversation has to stay balanced. But fairness goes both ways. In my opinion, if someone knowingly makes a false accusation that leads to an innocent person serving time, they should serve that same amount of time. And if no time was served, there should still Be a real consequence. At least one year in prison for false statements. Justice can't be one sided. Accountability has to match the damage caused.

The Goblet Squat is one of the foundational movements when it comes to kettlebell training.

Learning proper technique doesn’t begin when you start squatting. It starts with the setup. 

I like having the kettlebell handle in line with the midline of my foot (where my shoelaces start). There could be variation of this if you like it closer to your heel. 

From here, my glutes are above my knees, butt is still down and my chest is up. I break the kettlebell in half like I’m trying to split a piece of wood to engage my lats.

I pull the kettlebell into the front rack position, elbows down and arms are vertical not out. Drop your hips down and go all the way down until your thighs are parallel. Then use your feet to drive back up. 

You don’t want your spine rounded or your torso leaning forward, try and stay upright. Bracing your core and stacking your ribs should help with this.

caption:
Miso marinated cod, jasmine rice, and smashed cucumber Asian Salad 🐟

Cud Cooks x @alaskaseafooduk AD

Here is a delicious summer recipe; miso marinated cod served with jasmine rice and everyone's favourite Asian cucumber salad. It's healthy, full of protein, and comes together really quickly - the perfect summer dinner party dish. 

I've made this with the Miso Marinated Black Cod from @alaskaseafooduk. It's wild caught in Alaska, full of goodness, and comes pre-marinated in a delicious authentic Japanese miso sauce. Super easy to cook and takes a lot of the effort out. Full recipe below!

1. Smash 2 cucumbers with something heavy like a rolling pin. Chop these diagonally and place in a bowl with a generous pinch of fine salt. Mix and set aside for a minimum of 10 minutes to draw out the excess moisture
2. Start the cooking of your jasmine rice according to packet instructions
3. Put some oil in an oven-proof frying pan or skillet on a medium heat. Once hot, caramelise the Miso Marinated Black Cod from @alaskaseafooduk flesh side down for 1-2 minutes. Turn, and transfer the pan to a preheated 200C oven for c. 15 minutes
3. Whilst the fish is cooking, finish the salad. Drain the excess moisture from the cucumber, and finely slice 2 spring onions, 2 red chillies, and a small bunch of coriander stalks
4. In a bowl, add the cucumber, spring onions, red chillies, coriander, 4 finely diced garlic cloves, 2 tsp sugar, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tbsp sesame oil, 2 tbsp crispy chilli oil, and toasted sesame seeds. Mix well. Right before serving, add coriander leaves
5. Remove the fish from the oven, and plate on top of the rice. Serve the salad on the side. Serve with a wedge of lime.

#cooking #food #homemade #fish #recipe #foodtok #summer
subtitles: This is miso, marinated black cod, Jasmine rice and a banging smashed cucumber Asian salad. This is an awesome summer dish. Super healthy, packed full of protein, and it comes together really quickly. I love serving this in summer as an easy dinner party dish, and it also goes really well on a barbecue. For the salad, you smash and chop two cucumbers, cover them in salt and set them aside. This is to draw out the excess moisture. Whilst that's happening, we start the fish. The fish is black cod from Alaska. It's wild caught, it's delicious, and it comes in this authentic Japanese miso marinade. To cook these, you're gonna sear them flesh side down until you get a really nice caramelization, then transfer them to a 200 degree oven for about 15 minutes. Once those are cooking, you can make the salad. So chop up spring onions, chillies and coriander stalks. Drain the water from the cucumbers, then add garlic, coriander, rice vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, toasted sesame seeds, chilli oil, and finish with your fresh chillies and spring onion. Give that a mix, then you can remove your black cod from the oven, plate up some rice and get ready to serve.

caption:
CHARRED HISPI CABBAGE WITH MISO BUTTER AND SMOKED SALT 🥬🔥 RECIPE ⬇️

@cud_cooks x @maldonsalt AD

Smoky, savoury, and rich with umami - this simple side dish turns humble cabbage into something genuinely special. Charred hispi cabbage is basted in golden miso butter, finished with fresh lime, and brought to life with Maldon’s Smoked Sea Salt. A flavour bomb of smoke, tang, and depth. This is a perfect side dish, or a veggie alternative for a roast.

Slice 1 whole hispi cabbage in half lengthways. Heat some olive oil in a pan. Fry cut-side down over high heat for 4-5 mins until deeply browned and charred. Transfer to a 200°C oven and roast for 25-30 mins until tender.

Meanwhile, make the miso butter: mix 80g softened unsalted butter with 1 tbsp miso paste, the juice and zest of ½ lime, and a generous pinch of Maldon Smoked Sea Salt.

Return the cooked cabbage to the pan, add a large spoonful of miso butter, and baste until glossy and caramelised. Finish with extra miso butter, lime juice, lime zest, and another pinch of Maldon Smoked Sea Salt.

#cabbage #hispicabbage #miso #misobutter #maldonsalt
subtitles: This is hands down the best thing you can do with a cabbage. This one is charred, roasted and served with a miso butter and smoked salt. It's a perfect side dish or roast, and it only takes 30 minutes. You start with a hispi or pointed cabbage, slice it in half and then fry it flat side down, apply pressure downwards and cook until it's golden brown and charred at the edges. It should look like this and transfer to a 200 degree oven for about 30 minutes. Now combine butter, miso paste, lime juice and this smoked Maldon salt. This has a really deep, complex flavour. Mix that all up and you'll get this amazing miso and lime butter. Now you can remove the cabbage from the oven and put it in a pan with a spoon of that miso butter. Now you can gently fry it in all that amazing flavour and you'll end up with the best tasting cabbage of your life.

caption:
LEFTOVER TURKEY TOASTIE 🥪🔥 RECIPE ⬇️

#AD @cud_cooks x @Frank’s RedHot UK 

The ultimate leftover toastie: turkey, ham, stuffing, cranberry, melted brie or camembert, brussels, pancetta… all pressed together in golden, buttery tiger bread. Served with your Christmas gravy kicked up a notch using Frank’s RedHot for a gentle heat and tang that brings the whole thing to life.

Recipe:

Take two slices of tiger bread and spread cranberry sauce onto each.
On the first slice, layer: slices of brie or camembert, sliced brussels sprouts, cooked pancetta, 3 slices of turkey, salt + pepper, 3 slices of stuffing, and 3 slices of ham.
Top with the second slice of bread (cranberry-side down).
Heat butter in a pan over medium-low and toast the sandwich until golden brown and the cheese is melting.
For the gravy: reheat your leftover Christmas gravy and add Frank’s RedHot to spice up your side with a gentle heat and a tangy lift. Gauge quantities to taste - the gravy should have warmth, but not be overpowered.
Serve the toastie with the gravy for dipping.

#SpiceUpYourSide #FranksRedHot #toastie #christmas
subtitles: This is the ultimate leftover Turkey toastie. All of your Christmas leftovers used to make one of the best toasties you'll have in your life. I serve this with leftover gravy, kicked up a notch with Frank's Red Hot Sauce. This is one of the best things you'll do on Boxing Day. The beauty of this is you can pretty much put anything in it. I tend to go meat heavy with some nice gooey cheese. So you start by spreading a generous layer of cranberry sauce onto some tiger bread. Now layer up Camembert or Brie, add some leftover veg and pancetta. Now add slices of Turkey, season with salt and pepper, add stuffing, and then finish with slices of ham. Add more cranberry sauce and it's ready to toast. Now reheat your leftover gravy and add in Frank's Red Hot Sauce. This adds a really nice gentle heat and a bit of a Tang which pairs really well with the toastie. Now add butter to a pan on a medium low heat, add a weight and toast this on both sides until the cheese is melted and the bread is toasted. And there you go! That is how I spice up my leftovers.

caption:
Beef Wellington & Red Wine Jus 🥩🍷

Here’s a favourite centerpiece: Beef Wellington! Perfect for Christmas, this version features a 1kg beef fillet, a rich chestnut and mushroom duxelles with a hint of truffle oil, and golden puff pastry topped with a thyme-studded lattice. It’s paired with a rich, silky red wine jus for an unforgettable main dish. This recipe is part of my partnership with @robertwelchuk, featuring their Professional Knives, Campden Low Casserole Pot, and Campden Saucepan range – ideal for perfecting each step. Full recipe below.

Prepare the beef: Sear a 1kg center-cut beef fillet in the Campden Low Casserole Pot until golden on all sides (1-2 min per side). Cool, then brush with mustard.

Make the duxelles: In the same pot, cook 2 diced shallots in 30g butter and 2 tbsp truffle oil until softened. Add 500g finely chopped mushrooms, 100g finely chopped chestnuts, finely chopped thyme, rosemary and garlic. Cook until all moisture evaporates and cool.

Spinach crepes: Blanch 100g spinach and refresh in ice water. Blend spinach with 150g milk, then whisk into 2 eggs and 100g plain flour. Cook 4 thin crepes in a non-stick pan and cool.

Assemble: On cling film, lay the crepes flat, overlap with 8 slices of prosciutto, and spread duxelles to 0.5cm layer. Roll tightly around the beef using cling film, chill to set. Wrap the beef in puff pastry, add a lattice top (using a lattice cutter), and brush with egg wash. Garnish the gaps in the lattice with sprigs of thyme

Bake: Bake at 200°C for 30 minutes. Rest for 15 minutes.

Red wine jus: Roast 1kg beef bones, 2 marrow bones, 500g beef offcuts, and 4 shallots at 220°C until browned - around 30 mins. Add to a Campden Saucepan and add 500ml red wine, and bring to boil. Then add 1l water, thyme, rosemary, bay leaves, and peppercorns. Simmer for 3-4 hours, strain, and reduce to a silky jus that coats a spoon. Season to taste.

Slice the Wellington (1.5 inches), serve with jus, and enjoy this show-stopping dish!

#beef #wellington #cooking #recipe #winter
subtitles: This is beef Wellington with a bone marrow and red wine jus. This dish is the height of luxury. A perfectly cooked beef fillet wrapped in a Chestnut, mushroom and truffle duxelles and topped with a rich, silky bone marrow jus. This is the ultimate Christmas centerpiece. You start with the sauce by roasting beef bones off cuts and bone marrow until golden and caramelized. Put that in a pan with thyme, Rosemary and bay leaves. Deglaze with red wine, add water and simmer for 4 hours. Now season your fillet generously with salt and sear in a hot pan on all sides. Brush with mustard and leave to cool. Now to make the duxelles, you finely dice your shallots, put mushrooms into a food processor and blend until smooth. Then finely chop Rosemary and thyme. Now I'm going to elevate this with some whole chestnuts and a touch of truffle. Then we're gonna fry the shallots and herbs, add some garlic and cook the mushrooms until all of the moisture has evaporated. Then set aside to cool. Now we're going to make spinach crepes. This is a standard crepe recipe, but with the addition of blanched spinach, this gives a really unique green colour and a nice earthy flavour. Now layer the crepes prosciutto duxelles and then roll that around the beef fillet. Now roll that tightly in pastry, making sure there's no air pockets. This then goes into the oven at 200 degrees for about half an hour. While that rests, strain, reduce and season your sauce.

Duck breast // fig & port reduction 🦆🍷

subtitles: This technique will get you a perfect duck breast. Pair it with this fig and port reduction and you have an easy dish that looks impressive and tastes incredible. It all starts with a good quality duck breast. Score the fat without cutting the meat and season with salt. Lay fat side down in a cold pan. This is key. And gently render the fat on a medium heat until most of it's in the pan. You'll get this crispy skin. Then turn and sear the meat. Put in at 1:80 for eight minutes and then rest in a warm place. Whilst that's resting, you can gently soften shallots and figs in a touch of duck fat. Now deglaze the pan with port and add in honey, balsamic, thyme and chicken stock. Simmer this until the figs break down. Now strain through a fine sieve, reduce by half and finish with butter. You'll end up with this glossy sauce. Now carve your duck plate up and enjoy.

caption:
SLOW-BRAISED CHICKEN // CELERIAC MASH // TARRAGON CAPER SAUCE 🍋🍗 RECIPE ⬇️

Golden, crisp-skinned chicken legs slow-braised until tender, served over silky celeriac mash and finished with a bright tarragon, lemon and caper sauce.

Recipe (serves 3)

Peel and dice 2 whole celeriac into small 3-5mm squares. Melt 50g unsalted butter in a wide pan, add the celeriac with a generous pinch of salt, and cook over a medium heat for around 45 minutes, stirring frequently, until completely soft and most of the moisture has evaporated.
Stir through 150ml double cream and 100ml chicken stock, then blend until completely smooth. Check seasoning and keep warm.
Season 3 whole chicken legs  generously with salt and pepper. Heat 2 tbsp La Española Cooking Olive Oil in an ovenproof pan and sear the chicken skin-side down until deeply golden and crisp. Remove from the pan.
Lower the heat and soften 4 finely chopped garlic cloves. Add 4-5 thyme sprigs, then deglaze with 500ml chicken stock. Return the chicken to the pan, cover with a lid and cook in a 160°C oven for 45 minutes.
Remove the chicken and thyme stalks, then reduce the stock by roughly two-thirds. Stir through 2 tbsp crème fraîche and 1 tsp Dijon mustard, reducing again until the sauce coats the back of a spoon (add a splash more stock if needed).
Finish with the zest of ½ lemon, a squeeze of lemon juice, 3 tbsp chopped capers, and a handful of finely chopped fresh tarragon.
Spoon the celeriac mash onto plates, top with the chicken and sauce, and finish with a generous drizzle of La Española Extra Virgin Olive Oil.

#chicken #celeriac #recipe #dinner #meat
subtitles: This is a banging winter dish. This is slow braised chicken on a bed of silky celeriac mash with a rich sauce made from tarragon, capers and chicken stock. I like to finish this with a generous amount of high quality extra virgin olive oil. It's a decadent, comforting but really easy winter dish. It all starts with a humble celeriac. Get that peeled and cut it into small squares. Get a pan on the heat, add the celeriac, season and start softening. Whilst that's softening, season some chicken legs and add a generous amount of cooking olive oil to a pan. Now sear the chicken legs skin side down until they take on a really nice golden brown colour. Remove the legs from the pan and add in garlic and thyme. Deglaze with chicken stock. Put the legs back in the pan, add a lid and put in at 1:60 for 45 minutes. After about 45 minutes of gentle cooking, most of the water content will have left the celeriac. Add cream and stock quantities below, blend and you'll have an incredible smooth puree. Once your chicken is cooked, remove from the pan and then reduce the liquid by two thirds. Add creme fraiche and Dijon mustard. Now reduce until thick and finish with lemon zest, lemon juice, a generous amount of capers and fresh tarragon. Now mix this together, gently cook the sauce through and then serve a bit of celeriac, top with chicken and that sauce.

caption:
WHIPPED HONEY COFFEE // AFFOGATO ☕🍯🍦

This is literally the easiest dessert in the world, and probably the biggest taste-return on time taken.

This is Whipped Honey Coffee; a creamy, sweet coffee mixture served over vanilla ice cream.
	•	Whisk 150g runny honey with an electric whisk until thickened (around 5 minutes)
	•	Add 20g good quality instant coffee and 50ml hot water. Whisk for a further 5–10 minutes until thickened
	•	Optional - add dark chocolate shavings
	•	Serve over ice cream

#desserts #whippedcoffee #coffee #affogato #Recipe
subtitles: This dessert only uses two ingredients and takes 10 minutes to make. This is whipped honey coffee. Serve it with ice cream and it tastes like affogato. And if you're ever time pressure for dessert, this will save your day. You start with ingredient No. 1, runny honey, and whisk it until it has this thick consistency. Now add ingredient No. 2, instant coffee and a touch of hot water. And then continue to whisk until it looks like this. For an optional final touch, you can grate in dark chocolate, mix it in and that's dessert done.

caption:
MARRY ME MASH 🥔✨ Recipe below ⬇️

This is the ultimate recipe for luxurious mashed potato. Ultra-smooth, buttery, garlic-thyme infused, finished with white pepper and nutmeg. Make no mistake - this is pure indulgence, and it will make your guests so silent at the table.

Marry Me Mash:

Peel and cube 1kg Maris Piper potatoes. Add to cold salted water, bring to the boil, then simmer gently until completely tender. Drain and leave to steam dry for 20-30 minutes (this step is key for texture).
Meanwhile, gently simmer 200ml whole milk and 200ml double cream with 4 chopped garlic cloves and 3-4 thyme sprigs for 30 minutes to infuse. Strain and keep warm.
Pass the dried potatoes through a ricer, then fold through 150g melted butter. For extra smoothness, push through a fine mesh sieve.
Add the warm infused cream one ladle at a time until silky and smooth but still holding its shape. Season with fine salt, white pepper and a small grating of nutmeg. Taste and adjust.
Bonus recipe - Braised Short Rib (perfect with this mash):

Season 3-4 large beef short ribs generously with salt and pepper and sear in a hot casserole pot with 1 tbsp oil until deeply browned. Remove.
In the same pot soften 1 diced onion, 2 diced celery sticks and 2 diced carrots. Add 2 tbsp tomato purée, 3 sliced garlic cloves, 3 thyme sprigs and 2 bay leaves. Deglaze with 500ml red wine, reduce slightly, then add enough beef stock (around 750ml-1L) to fully submerge the ribs.
Return the ribs, cover and cook at 130°C for 4 hours until spoon tender. Remove the ribs, strain and remove the fat from the sauce (use a separator jug if you have one). Pass through a fine sieve and then reduce it until glossy and thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Return the ribs to the sauce and baste.
Silky mash. Sticky, rich beef. Absolute comfort food - elevated.

#mash #shortrib #cooking #recipe #food
subtitles: This is a recipe for something I make called Marry Me Mash. It's the kind of mashed potato you'd find in a French cookbook from 100 years ago. Total indulgence and decadence, and the most incredible base for slow cooked dishes like short ribs, ox cheek and brisket. This mash takes 6 steps, each one important but each very simple. It all starts with getting the right potatoes. These are Maris Pipers and they seem to have just about the right starch content. Step 1 is cooking the potatoes. Put them in a pan, add cold water, simmer until soft and then steam dry on a tray to get rid of excess water. step 2 is infusing equal parts milk and cream with garlic and thyme by gently simmering. Whilst that's infusing, step 3 is passing the potatoes through a ricer to get us near the final texture that we want. Now, step 4 is turning through a generous amount of melted butter. At this stage the mash will be smooth, but not totally smooth. So step 5 is passing this through a fine sieve. This is optional, but it gives an amazing texture. Now step 6 is slowly incorporating the infused milk and cream one glazal at a time until you achieve your desired texture. Finish with a generous amount of salt, white pepper and a touch of nutmeg. Warm through and enjoy.

caption:
PERFECT PORK BELLY 🐖🔥 RECIPE ⬇️

Crispy skin, tender meat, caramelised fennel, and a rich cider gravy - this is the perfect pork belly. Slow-roasted for tenderness, finished at high heat for crackling, and served with roasted fennel, shallots, apples, and thyme.

Recipe below ⬇️

Pork: Place a 2.5kg pork belly in the fridge uncovered overnight. Next day, wrap foil so it covers just the meat, leaving skin exposed. Brush with olive oil, season with salt, and roast at 140°C for 2½ hours.
Veg: In a casserole pot, combine 2 quartered fennel bulbs, 6 halved shallots, 1 halved garlic bulb, 2 apples (cut into sixths), thyme, fennel seeds, salt, pepper, and olive oil. Roast for 1 hour in the same oven.
Combine: Pour pork juices into the veg, then roast both together at 240°C for 30-40 mins to crisp the skin. Remove the pork and rest uncovered
Gravy: Deglaze the casserole with 1-2 bottles cider, boil, strain, and reduce until glossy.
Serve the veg in a dish, spoon over the cider gravy, and slice the pork to serve on top.

#porkbelly #meat #roast #dinner #recipe
subtitles: This is perfect pork belly. This is how you get flawless, crunchy crackling on top of the juiciest meat you will ever have. This one is served with slow roasted apples, fennel and shallots and is covered in lashings of rich cider gravy. It all starts with high quality butcher sourced pork belly left uncovered in the fridge overnight. Wrap tin foil around just the meat and then brush with olive oil and salt. Roast at ONE FORTYC for two and a half hours. Whilst that's roasting, you can roughly chop up the vegetables. I'm using an autumnal mix of apples, fennel, shallots and garlic. You can then layer these into the base of a casserole pan and top with fresh thyme, fennel seeds and olive oil and put in the oven. After two and a half hours, the pork will be cooked but not crackled. Pour the juices on the veg, remove the foil from the pork and put both back in the oven for 30 minutes at 2 40C. Now your vegetables should look like this. Remove the veg and deglaze the pan with cider. Then pass the liquid through a sieve and add it back into the pan. Turn on the heat and reduce to a thick consistency. Your pork will now look like this crispy, cracking, perfectly cooked meat. You can now layer up your roasted vegetables and gravy and enjoy some of the best pork belly of your life.

caption:
PERFECT ROAST CHICKEN WITH GARLIC & TARRAGON MAYONNAISE 🍗✨ RECIPE ⬇️

Crisp, golden skin, juicy meat, rich gravy, and the most addictive homemade garlic and tarragon mayonnaise - this is the ultimate roast chicken. Simple, classic, and made even better with Maldon Garlic Sea Salt.

Recipe:
Take 1 whole quality chicken. Stuff the cavity with 2 shallots, 2 garlic cloves, a few sprigs of thyme, and a generous pinch of Maldon Sea Salt. Pat the skin dry, brush all over with olive oil, and season generously with Maldon Garlic Sea Salt.

In an oven-safe pan, add 4 peeled shallots, 4 garlic cloves, sprigs of thyme and rosemary, and a drizzle of olive oil. Place a wire rack over the top and set the chicken on it - this lets the bird crisp all over while the juices drip into the pan. Roast at 180°C for around 1 hour 15 minutes, or until golden and cooked through.

Garlic & Tarragon Mayonnaise:
In a food processor, combine 2 egg yolks, 1 tbsp Dijon mustard, juice of ½ lemon, 2 tbsp chardonnay vinegar, a pinch of caster sugar, a pinch of Maldon Garlic Sea Salt, and 1 grated garlic clove. Blend briefly. With the motor running, slowly drizzle in 150g vegetable oil and 100g virgin rapeseed oil until thick and glossy. Fold through a handful of finely chopped fresh tarragon.

Gravy:
Once the chicken is cooked, rest it in a warm place. Pour 500ml cider into the roasting pan to deglaze, scraping up all the caramelised bits. Add 500ml chicken stock and bring to a boil. Sieve into a saucepan, add 2-3 knobs of butter, and reduce until it coats the back of a spoon.

Carve the chicken, serve with the gravy and a generous spoonful of the garlic and tarragon mayonnaise. Heaven.

subtitles: There is no better meal in the world than this. This is a perfectly roasted chicken served with a homemade garlic and tarragon mayonnaise and ladles of rich, decadent gravy. It's easy, it's cheap and it all starts with a high quality chicken. Stuff your chicken with shallots and thyme, brush with olive oil and coat it in this garlic Maldon sea salt. This gives the skin the most incredible flavour. Next, place shallots, garlic and fresh herbs in a pan, place the chicken on a rack and put in at ONE EIGHTYC for an hour and 15. Whilst that's roasting, we can make the garlic mayonnaise. The full recipe is in the caption, but it's very straightforward and the key is again using that garlic Maldon sea salt. The mayonnaise is a perfect accompaniment for the chicken and will come together into this thick, silky consistency. Then we chop up fresh tarragon and turn that through the mayonnaise. Once the chicken is out of the oven, set aside to rest and add cider to the pan. The cider will deglaze the pan and bring up all that incredible flavour. Then to make the gravy, we pass that through a sieve, put it back in a pan, add butter and then reduce to the right consistency. Now that chicken is rested, you can go ahead and carve and you've got one of the best meals of your life.

caption:
CHINESE STEAMED EGG 🥚🌶️ RECIPE ⬇️

One of my all time favourite breakfasts. Super simple, packed with protein, and absolutely delicious. 

- Crack 3 eggs into a bowl, weigh them (write it down), and mix
- Zero the scales, and then add warm (not hot!) chicken stock until you have a ratio of 1 part egg to 1.5 parts stock (take the weight of your eggs and multiply by 1.5, and add that amount of stock. For example if you have 170g eggs, you need 255g stock)
- Gently combine without causing bubbles, and pass through a sieve
- Heat a bowl in a steamer (critical!). Then add eggs to the bowl, cling film the top, and steam for 10 minutes. Turn heat off and sit in steamer for further 5 minutes
- Slice the cooked egg, and add sesame oil, sesame seeds, chilli oil, soy sauce, and spring onion

#egg #breakfast #china #cooking #steamedegg
subtitles: This is a really unique breakfast. It's healthy, high in protein and absolutely delicious. This is Chinese steamed egg. All it takes is eggs, chicken stock and a bit of technique and you've got something really amazing. First, crack three eggs into a bowl, weigh them and mix. Now zero the scales and add warm chicken stock in a ratio of 1 part egg to 1.5 parts stock. Now gently combine the egg and the stock and then pass them through a sieve to remove any lumps and ensure a silky final texture. Put a bowl into your steamer to get it hot. This is critical. And then gently pour in the mixture. Now add cling film, place it back in the pan and steam for 10 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave it for a further five minutes. Once cooked, you can slice it and add your favourite toppings like soy sauce, sesame and chilli oil.

caption:
A BRITISH CLASSIC - FISH & CHIPS 🇬🇧🐟🍟

@ed.cudlipp x @Waitrose & Partners AD

There are few things better than proper fish and chips. For this one I went all in and made everything from scratch using ingredients from Waitrose - crispy, golden cod, double-fried chips, homemade tartare sauce, all finished with Waitrose Chip Shop Curry Sauce. The cod came fresh from the Waitrose fish counter (all Waitrose fish is responsibly sourced).

Recipe (serves 2):

- Peel 5–6 Maris Piper potatoes, cut into chunky chips and rinse until water runs clear. Add to salted cold water, bring to the boil and cook ~7 mins until just tender.
- Drain, steam dry, then fry at 135°C for ~6 mins. Remove and cool completely.
- Tartare sauce: make mayo by blending 2 egg yolks, 1 tsp Dijon mustard, ½ lemon juice, 2 tbsp chardonnay vinegar, pinch sugar and salt, then slowly add 150g veg oil and 100g rapeseed oil. Mix 6 tbsp with chopped cornichons, capers, lemon juice, parsley and tarragon. Chill.
- Batter: whisk 200g flour, 100g cornflour, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp baking powder and salt. Add 400ml cold sparkling water to form a loose batter.
- Lightly flour and batter two cod fillets from the Waitrose fish counter.
- Fry chips again at 185°C for ~5 mins until golden and crisp. Season well.
- Fry fish at 180°C for 5–8 mins until crisp and golden. Season.
- Warm Waitrose Chip Shop Curry Sauce and serve with fish, chips and tartare.

Golden fish. Proper chips. Curry sauce on the side. Exactly how it should be.

Add a generous layer of chips, put the fish on top, heat your curry sauce and serve.

caption:
HOT HONEY WINGS 🔥🍯 RECIPE ⬇️

Crispy, sticky, spicy, and sweet - these Hot Honey Wings are dangerously addictive. Glazed in melted butter, honey, and hot sauce, and finished with Maldon’s Chilli Sea Salt for a fiery, flaky kick. Perfect for game day, dinner, or just a Friday night craving.

Recipe:
For 20 winglets (whole chicken wings, cut in half) (serves 2), toss the wings in 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp garlic powder, 1 tbsp onion powder, 1 tbsp smoked paprika, and a generous pinch of Maldon Chilli Sea Salt. Arrange on a wire rack over a tray and bake at 170°C for 1 hour, until golden and crisp.

For the hot honey glaze, melt 50g butter with 4 tbsp honey, 4 tbsp Frank’s Hot Sauce, 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar, and a pinch of Maldon Chilli Sea Salt. Stir to combine over low heat.

Once the wings are cooked, toss them generously in the sauce until coated and sticky. Finish with fresh lemon juice, chopped chives, and an extra sprinkle of Maldon Chilli Sea Salt.

#wings #food #recipe #chicken #cooking
subtitles: These are hot honey chicken wings. Spicy, sweet, fall off the bone chicken wings coated in a thick honey butter glaze and finished with fresh herbs, lemon and chili salt. These are epic. And it all starts with a humble chicken wing. First, lay out your wings and make sure they're dry. Then put them in a bowl and coat with oil, garlic powder, smoked paprika, onion powder and this chilli Maldon sea salt. This salt is full of Aleppo pepper and bird's eye chilli and it gives a really nice kick to the wings. Once they're coated, place them on a rack and bake for one hour at ONE SEVENTYC. Now the sauce is butter, loads of honey and Frank's hot sauce. Gently heat and then add cider vinegar and more Chilli Maillard salt that will come together into this sticky glaze. Once the wings are done, put them in the glaze, shake the pan, finish with lemon and you've got some incredible chicken wings.

#school #collegetips #yoonchae #whimsical #lifeadvice
subtitles: The secret to not giving a flying freak about what people think and just living your life is to be whimsical. And consider yourself lucky bc today i'm gonna teach you exactly how. And the first one is something that I do all the time. So good. Is to leave tiny surprises for people. This is golden rule number one, okay? Whimsy multiplies when it spreads. So just to give you a couple examples of things that i've personally done. Put a tiny handwritten comment inside a library book. Randomly buying flowers just because they're pretty and not for any special occasions, and leaving some on random people's desks. Anonymously drawing your friend a tiny doodle. Something that reminds you of them. Or just like a silly inside joke. Visiting your professors, going to their office hours with a special tea bag or like a coffee. I've also done like a bookmark. Nothing expensive. Say something like, oh, I saw this and thought of your class. Writing letters for people you feel grateful for. Cause I know if someone else did those things for me. I would personally feel so grateful and really happy. And so I would always try to do those things for other people. At the end of the day, it never hurts to be sweet. My number two tip is to dress for a secret theme every day of the week. Choose a hidden aesthetic and stick to it. I tried this on my family vaca last year, and it made the trip so much more fun. For example, you can dress up as a french bookstore owner, a victorian child, studio ghibli background character, italian summer vacation. I mean, no one has to know, but it just makes walking around feel so much more fun. My third tip is to create beautiful, useless collections. If you're also a perfectionist like me, it trains you to be less goal oriented. Because I would always think about my next big thing. Everything I did had to serve a purpose, and that's just not healthy. So you wanna collect things purely because they're delightful, they're beautiful, for no apparent reason. You're just kind of wasting your time, but you're happy! I started collecting tiny seashells, really smooth stones, airplane boarding passes or train tickets, cafe sugar packets from different cafe shops. I love cafe hopping. Napkins with doodles and candy wrappers. So there you go. These are all my tips to moving in silence and whimsy. Try these out and you'll thank me later.

caption:
nothing is ever that serious 
#school #collegetips #yoonchae #whimsical #lifeadvice
subtitles: Being whimsical does not mean changing your whole character to do big, dramatic things. But it's about tiny, playful disruptions to daily, mundane life that make the day feel like a story or a movie rather than just a checklist. So if you also just wanna stop giving a freak and just start living, here's what you need to do. Number one, turn your errands into missions. Yes, I know that not everyday is interesting, but what you can do is give your boring tasks a narrative. So instead of just saying, oh yeah, i'm just going to the grocery store to pick up a couple of stuff, you can say, today i'm on the quest to find the most beautiful vegetable. You'll actually go and try to accomplish this mission. You'll be so surprised by how much this changes your mood. Number two is pretty specific, which is to adopt a signature drink. Pick one drink that you can romanticize. For example, iced matcha latte in the afternoons, or sparkling water plus lime in a very fancy glass, or hot chocolate at night. Whatever it is, you adopt this character and the role is to drink it slowly and intentionally. Number three can sound a little hard, but it's actually so rewarding and so worth it. Is to talk to strangers in tiny ways. Not deep conversations, just playful human interactions. Little moments. For example, compliment someone's shoes, or ask a barista their favourite drink on the menu. Tell Someone. Their dog looks cute. Whatever. A big part of being whimsical is to create those spontaneous moments that you just don't know what can come out of. And those little, tiny interactions can help you come up with responses faster and just train your brain to be more witty. So, yes, there you go. Do these if you want to lead an interesting life. And thank me later.

caption:
It’s not over. The academic comeback starts NOW
#college #studytok #studytips #examseason #yoonchae
subtitles: Your semester is almost ending, so if you want to lock in an A, here's some non obvious things that can actually move your grade. Number one, pull up your past exams right now and analyse them. If it's cumulative, what topics repeat? What are the formats like? And how do they word questions so you're studying the test maker and not just the content. And with that, the second step is to go to office hours instead of just asking, oh, like what should I study? Instead, ask: if students usually lose points, Where is it? Or something like: what separates an A from a B on this exam? And I guarantee you the professors will literally tell you, exactly how to win. And the third step is to build a mistake bank. Write down every question you got wrong. Plus why. Is it because you misread the question? Because you didn't know the concept itself? Or is it because you ran out of time? Simply doing more problems is not gonna help you get better grades if you don't know how to fix them. And then now this step is so good is to pre write your exam language, especially for writing based classes. Just have two to three flexible thesis statements or frameworks ready during the exam. You're confident that you're adapting from some something that's good because you've studied through before and not just coming up with something from scratch. This saves so much time it's actually unfair. And finally, study like the exam format. For multiple choice, drill speed and pattern recognition. For essays, practice structuring fast. For problem solving. Timed reps. so don't study passively if your exam is active. best of luck! And just remember, finals are not about knowing everything, but knowing what matters.

subtitles: I thought working in finance meant I was protected from AI, but then I read this paper and realised I'm one of the most exposed people in the room. Anthropic just released a research paper on which jobs AI is actually replacing and which one it can replace in theory, and things are not looking good for me. They introduced this new metric called observed exposure which measures what AI could theoretically handle. You can see in the blue area versus what it actually handles today in the red area. As an example, in computer and math jobs, AI could theoretically handle 95% of tasks. The cloud only covers about 32% of doors. Similarly, in office and admin jobs, 94% of tasks could be theoretically covered, but only 42% are covered today. They also released a list of top 10 occupations most exposed and surprise, surprise, computer programmers are on top with 74% exposed. Next in line are customer service workers with 70%, data entry workers with 67%, medical record specialist with 66.7% and the list goes on. But even financial and investment analysts are on the list with 57%. Here's the pattern that stood out to me. The most at risk jobs are white collar, require higher education, well paid and also 16% more likely to be female. These are not factory floor jobs, these are the jobs that we were told are safe. I work in investment banking but my job is very much affected by this because I write the algorithms that trade on the stock market, so I'm literally at the intersection of two of the most affected areas. But it's not just people. Mid career AI can replace juniors a lot more easily than someone in the decision making role. Hiring for people aged 22 to 25 in the exposed areas has slowed down, so there's no mass layoffs, but fewer people are getting through the door. Now there's a silver lining. Well, kind of. There's no major spike in unemployment yet, but we are still very much at the early stages. Chat GPT only launched in late 2022, barely three years ago, and look how far we've come. #investing #personalfinance #investingforbeginners #learnontiktok #moneytok
subtitles: I would never put money into an E T F. Without checking these five things first. And if you're new here, I'm Emmy. I've spent 11 years in investment banking and built a 300 K portfolio in my 20s. Number one is annualised performance. Basically how well the fund has done on average each year. Of course, everyone says past performance does not predict the future, but it does tell you how the fund has behaved in different market conditions. That's a very important benchmark when you wanna compare to other E T F's. No.2 is dividend frequency. E T S can be distributing when the dividends are paid out in cash, or accumulating when the dividends are automatically reinvested into the fund. I personally almost always go for accumulating because that way I can take full advantage of compounding without me having to lift a finger. Next off, we have volatility. This measures how much the value of the fund goes up and down over time. The number to look for is called beta. Beta of 1 means it moves in line with the market. Below 1 means it's calmer, and above 1, it's bigger. Swings in both directions. So for example, S M H, the semiconductor E T F, has a beta of 1.5. So if the S M P. 500 drops 10%, S M H. Could drop 15%. In general, lower volatility E T F's are considered less risky. But keep in mind that less risk Often comes with lower potential returns. No.. 4 is the funds top allocations. Knowing which sectors and regions dominate the fund helps you understand if it's diversified enough, which is directly linked to how much risk you're taking on. And finally, No. 5 is the expense ratio. This is the money you pay every year for holding the fund. It's usually taken automatically so you don't see a separate charge on your statement. It's charged by the fund manager to cover things like running the fund, checking the index, and compliance. For E. T. F's, anything below zero point 20% is considered cheap. Many broad market E. T. F's sit between 0.05 and 0.3%. It might sound small, but on the long term even a difference between 0.2 and 0.3% can cost you thousands of pounds because it compounds every year. So those are the five key things I check before investing into any E. T. F. If you found this useful, drop a comment with the E. You're currently looking at and follow for more.

It's a tax free investment account where you can invest up to £20,000 every year and you don't need to pay any tax on your returns. Now, what do you actually invest in? subtitles: It's Friday, so let's go over another financial term. This week, let's dive into the sunk cost fallacy. A sunk cost is a cost that has been incurred that cannot be recovered. The fallacy comes into play because even though it can't be recovered, because we've invested so much time, money, energy, whatever into this thing, we keep investing more and more in the hopes that one day it'll pay off. But as you can imagine, we just keep losing more and more. We often think about this when it comes to business. However, it can play a huge role in our personal finances and our relationships. subtitles: What is short selling? A lot of people can get confused by this, but today my goal is to help you understand. Let's say in a hypothetical world, you went to the grocery store on a Thursday and saw that they were selling a large case of Coca Cola for $25. However, you know that on Fridays, they marked the case down 50% to $12 and ¢50. Let's say in this hypothetical world, the grocery store will allow you to borrow the case of Coke without actually having to buy it. You'll just have to make sure that you give it back to them. Well, if you could borrow a case of Coke on Thursday, you could sell it to someone for $25. So now you have $25, but no case of Coke to give back to the grocery store. So what do you do now? You wait till Friday when the Coke is 50% off, to be able to buy it at $12 and ¢50 and give that case back to the grocery store. Now you don't know the grocery store anything, and you made $12 and ¢50 in the process. While this doesn't work with grocery stores, in the real world, it does work with stocks, and it's called short selling. If you believe that a stock price is going to go down, you can borrow it and sell it to someone while it's still high, and then when it's low, buy it back to be able to give Back to the brokerage firm that you borrowed it from. Exactly the same as the grocery store example.

•once the pan is warmed up add the diced chicken breasts
•season the chicken with onion powder, garlic powder, Tony’s, paprika, Dan-o’s butter dust

•once cheese is melted add in the noodles and give it a good mix

Replying to @MH~KillerK Brown stew chicken recipe 🇯🇲🍗

Ingredients:  
- chicken (skinless and boneless thighs/drumsticks)
- Garlic and ginger paste (or 3 garlic cloves and a ginger thumb)
- 2tbsp green seasoning 
- 2 spring onions, diced
- 1 red bell pepper, sliced
- 1 green bell pepper, sliced
- 1 scotch bonnet 
- 1 red onion, diced 
- Fresh thyme 
- 2tbsp ketchup
- 2 chicken stock cubes 
- Drizzle of browning 
- 2tbsp brown sugar 
- Olive oil 
- 1tbsp jerk bbq sauce 

Seasonings: 
All purpose, smoked paprika, garlic granules, liquid maggi 

Method: 

1. Wash and dry your chicken. Remove and skin/bones if still on. 
2. Marinade the chicken with the seasonings, oil, a crumbled stock cube, browning, peppers, onions and thyme. The longer you leave it , the better it will taste.
3. Heat oil in a pan. Add brown sugar and let it caramelise until it's dark.
4. Add the chicken and cook until it's caramelised on each side then remove and set aside. 
5. In the same pan, fry the veg mix for 3 mins.
6. Return chicken to the pan. Add stock, thyme, scotch bonnet, ketchup and jerk BBQ sauce. 
7. Cover and simmer 45–60 mins.
8. Serve with rice and peas or white rice, plantain and slaw 🥰

Replying to @hotwasabi99 Mango jerk inspired spatchcock chicken recipe 🍗🥭🥥

Chicken ingredients: 
- 1 whole chicken, spatchcocked 
- 2 white onions
- Large knob of ginger
- 4 garlic cloves
- 3 tbsp mango chutney
- Juice of 2 limes
- 2tbsp olive oil 
- 2 tbsp brown sugar
- dry jerk rub
- wet jerk marinade
- Handful fresh thyme
- Sea salt
- Honey (for drizzling before roasting)

Coconut jerk gravy ingredients: 
- 1 can of coconut milk
- Knob of butter 
- Fresh thyme 
- Leftover chicken marinade 
- Juices from chicken 

Method

	1.	Clean and spatchcock your chicken.
    2. Add onions, ginger, garlic, mango chutney, lime juice, olive oil, brown sugar, dry jerk rub, wet jerk marinade and fresh thyme to a blender. Blend until smooth.
    3. Preheat oven to 190°C fan (210°C conventional).
    4. Put some water at the bottom of a large tray (this is to stop the marinade from burning), then add the spatchcock chicken, score it and massage the marinade all over the chicken, getting under the skin where possible. Cover and marinate for as long as possible - overnight for best flavour.
	4.	Before roasting, sprinkle extra dry jerk rub, sea salt and fresh thyme over the chicken, then drizzle with honey.
	5.	Roast for 50–60 minutes, basting halfway with pan juices, until golden, sticky and cooked through (internal temp 75°C). Rest for 10 minutes before carving.
	6.	For the gravy, pour the chicken tray juices into a saucepan. Add leftover marinade, coconut milk, thyme and butter. Simmer on medium heat for 10–15 minutes, stirring until thick and glossy.
	7.	Taste and adjust seasoning if needed, then serve poured over the chicken or on the side.

Replying to @Caroline ✨ PEACH COBBLER RECIPE 🍑🍨

INGREDIENTS
✨ 2 cans sliced peaches (drained) / 4 peaches, peeled and sliced 
✨ 120ml water
✨ 100g brown sugar
✨ 50g granulated sugar 
✨ 1 tsp cinnamon
✨ 1 tsp nutmeg 
✨ 2 tbsp vanilla essence 
✨ Juice from 1 small lemon 
✨ 1 tsp cornflour mixed with a little bit of water to make a slurry 
✨ 50g butter 

Cobbler topping: 
✨ 120g unsalted butter, melted 
✨ 150g self-raising flour
✨ 150g caster sugar
✨ 240ml milk
✨ Pinch of salt
✨ 2 tsp vanilla essence 

METHOD
1. Heat oven to 180°C.
2. Coat baking dish in butter.
3. Simmer peaches, liquid, sugar, nutmeg, cinnamon, vanilla, lemon & cornflour for 5 mins on a low heat until saucy.
4. Mix the cobbler topping ingredients, then leave to rest for 5 minutes and don't stir again. 
5. Pour the peach mixture into the baking dish, then spoon the cobbler topping on top. 
6. Bake in the oven for 30mins until golden and bubbling.
7. Leave the cobbler to rest for a few minutes, then serve with ice cream (I suggest salted caramel 🤤)

ROAST POTATOES RECIPE 🥔

- Potatoes (Maris Piper or King Edward)
- Beef stock cube 
- Oil of choice (I use goose fat or beef dripping)
- Fresh rosemary 
- Garlic cloves (skin on) 
- Sea salt flakes 
- Pepper
- Garlic granules
- Aromat 

1. Preheat oven to 200c. 
2. Peel and cut your potatoes into quarters and add them to a pan with boiling water, salt and beef stock. Parboil for around 8-10mins until the potatoes are soft enough to be pierced easily (but not falling apart).
3. Add the oil to your baking tray and heat it up in the oven for 5mins. 
4. Drain the potatoes and shake them in a pan to rough up the edges (this makes them fluffy). 
5. When the oil is piping hot, add the potatoes and garlic cloves to the tray, then top with salt and pepper. (Make sure you turn the potatoes over so they're coated in the oil). Roast for 45-55mins. 
6. Half way through cooking, remove the potatoes, turn them over and crush them lightly (this helps them to be crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside). Add your aromat, garlic granules, fresh rosemary and pop them back in the oven for the remaining time, then enjoy 🥰

If you’re trying to break into asset management, investment banking, or financial markets, these are some of the most common terms you’ll hear every day.

1️⃣ Yield
Yield is the return you earn on an investment, usually expressed as a percentage.
For bonds, it’s the income you receive relative to the price you paid.

Example:
If bond yields go up, bond prices usually go down.

2️⃣ Spread
A spread is the difference between two yields.
In credit markets, it’s often the difference between a corporate bond yield and a government bond yield.

Spreads help investors measure risk and relative value.

3️⃣ Long
Going long means you’re betting an asset will increase in value.
Example: buying a stock or bond because you believe the price will rise.

4️⃣ Short
Going short means you’re betting an asset will fall in value.
Investors borrow the asset, sell it, and aim to buy it back later at a lower price.

5️⃣ Liquidity
Liquidity refers to how easily you can buy or sell an asset without affecting the price.

Highly liquid markets = easier trading.
Low liquidity = wider spreads and more volatility.

If you want to work in asset management or the buy side, these terms will come up constantly in meetings, research, and interviews.
